trial_court: Additional Sessions Judge, Paonta Sahib, District Sirmaur, Himachal Pradesh, case No.67/2021
facts_of_case: Petitioner (husband) challenged an order granting interim maintenance to respondent (wife) in the tune of Rs.10,000/- per month. Parties attempted amicable settlement but ultimately decided to settle their dispute by filing a joint petition for mutual divorce under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: There is no requirement of 'cooling period' of six months in cases where marriage has broken beyond repair and there is no possibility of parties living together.
legal_principles.held: This Court taking note of various judgments of Hon'ble Apex court has repeatedly held that there is no requirement of 'cooling period' of six months in the cases where marriage has broken beyond repair and there is no possibility of parties living together.
cited_cases: Bharti Kapoor v. Des Raj, CMPMO No. 271 of 2017, decided on 31.10.2018
keywords: no possibility of parties living together

legal_principles.principle: The statutory period of six months as envisaged under Section 13B of the Act for grant of divorce by way of mutual consent can be waived when there is no possibility of rapprochement and marriage has broken beyond repair.
legal_principles.held: Statutory period of six months as envisaged under Section 13B of the Act for grant of divorce by way of mutual consent can be waived, especially when there is no possibility of rapprochement of the parties and marriage has broken beyond repair.
cited_cases: Veena vs. State (Government of NCT of Delhi) and another, (2011)14 SCC 614
Priyanka Khanna v. Amit Khanna, (2011) 15 SCC 612

outcome.final_order: Parties agreed to file a joint petition for mutual divorce and settled their dispute amicably. Petitioner (husband) shall pay Rs.13,50,000/- towards permanent alimony to respondent (wife).

keywords: Section 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C.
use_for_drafting: family law disputes in Himachal Pradesh
